issues.title: Unjustified zero-central-frequency range identity

failure_location.quote: Using the range identity of \cite{GGH2022} (see also Theorem A. 1. in the appendix) we obtain the relation

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\real T$ and $\ima T$ are both one-to-one
one deduces from these new measurement data with $k_{\min}=-k_{\max}$ that $\kappa=0$ and $K=k_{\max}$

issues.failure_explanation: The old Appendix Theorem A.1 requires both Re T and Im T to be one-to-one. The paper explicitly uses kappa=0, and the multiplication formula oT with real S then makes Im T_epsilon the zero operator on a nontrivial source space, so it is not one-to-one. Consequently, the invocation in the proof of RH does not establish the range identity at that endpoint. The revised theorem permits Im T=0 and identifies a separate justification for that case.
issues.overall_effect: For the zero-centered frequency construction, RH and every subsequent exact-range and Picard argument relying on it lack the stated range-identity input. This root does not affect the nonzero-kappa branch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Appendix Theorem A.1 the standard self-adjoint alternative in which Im T=0, with an appropriate proof or citation. At κ=0, verify at each truncated and finite-dimensional invocation that Re T=T is injective and |Re T| is coercive from the positive lower bound on |S|; then RIeps, RIN, RH, and the existing dependent Picard chain remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof genuinely invokes a theorem outside its hypotheses, so this is not a typo. However, κ=0 is a standard self-adjoint middle-operator case requiring only a local replacement of the cited range-identity input and routine checks. It preserves the frequency regime, method, conclusions, and all dependent guarantees without a new construction or proof architecture.

issues.title: Undefined time variable in the support lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The lemma has no parameter t among its inputs. Definition def:L contains the phase c^{-1} hat{x}·y-t_0, so its inverse-Fourier support is shifted by -t_0. The proof of lem3.4 also states and uses precisely the t_0-shifted interval. Thus the printed t is undefined and incompatible with the construction, while t_0 is uniquely forced.
issues.overall_effect: Read literally, the support lemma has an undefined shift and cannot supply the t_0-dependent support inclusion used in the reverse implication of lem3.4 and its downstream chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the undefined shift −t by −t_0 at both endpoints of equation (rl-f). No downstream statement or proof step requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: Definition (def:L) contains only t_0, and the proof and use in Lemma 3.4 already employ exactly the t_0-shifted interval. The old source therefore uniquely forces this transcriptional correction, and an intended reader can continue without repairing any mathematical inference.

issues.title: False exact-range characterization of pointwise tests

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Fix an admissible direction, eta, K>0, and z in the stated strip. If the old L^2(D) operator satisfied Lw(k)=exp(-ikb) on (0,K), then boundedness of D gives w in L^1(D), so Lw has an entire extension and tends to zero as real |k| tends to infinity. Equality on the open frequency interval would extend analytically to all real k, contradicting the unit modulus of the exponential. Thus the forward implication is false. Membership in finite-dimensional ranges and convergence of operators or ranges cannot yield the claimed exact membership in Range(L).
issues.overall_effect: The exact pointwise range criterion, and therefore the Picard indicators and strip, excitation-time, hull, and uniqueness results built on that criterion, are not established in the old L^2 framework.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the L²(D) factorization but replace the pure exponential by the Fourier transform of a smooth bump of radius r centered at b=c^{-1}hat{x}·z−η. A cross-sectional construction gives an L²(D) preimage whenever the bump support is compactly contained in the projected source interval, while the support lemma gives the converse; hence b is in that interval exactly when such membership holds for some r>0. Aggregate the Picard indicators over a sequence r tending to zero and propagate this replacement through all listed strip, excitation-time, hull, and uniqueness results.
issues.why_classification: No local correction can put the pure exponential in Range(L) in the old L² framework: analytic continuation and real-axis decay rule it out even for interior points. Nevertheless, localized L²-admissible tests yield a recognizably comparable shrinking-radius range criterion while leaving the factorization and range identity intact, and the exact geometric and uniqueness guarantees survive after aggregation over radii. Constructing that criterion and revising the dependent indicators is contained but nontrivial work, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.
